Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: Standalone holding company basis, p.6-8. No revenue (holding company; other operating income and finance income/dividends are the only inflows) -- revenue/cost_of_sales/gross_profit left blank as not applicable. Interest-bearing loans and borrowings are entirely non-current (310,000); no short-term borrowings line at Company level this quarter. capex = 0, no PPE/intangible purchases this quarter (only an equity-accounted-investee investment of 80,000, shown in cash_from_investing). total_liabilities = total assets (15,314,681) minus total equity (14,789,326).

Cinnamon Hotels & Resorts operator, subsidiary of JKH (Leisure segment). Consolidated basis. p.1 income statement, p.3 balance sheet, p.4 cash flow (quarter-isolated). tax_expense entered as -239,884: the income statement line is a 'Tax reversal' (credit), i.e. profit_after_tax = profit_before_tax minus a negative tax_expense = profit_before_tax + 239,884, which reconciles to the disclosed loss for the period. minority_interest = non-controlling interests' share of the loss for the period (-2,988), not a balance-sheet NCI equity balance. total_liabilities = 42,687,667 per the operating-segment note's Group Total Liabilities line (matches total assets 76,610,946 minus total equity 33,923,279). Operating segments are Sri Lanka and Maldives; Maldives revenue fell 24.2% YoY (3,976,146 to 3,012,445) and its segment loss widened from Rs.87mn to Rs.1.18bn, the dominant driver of the Group loss -- consistent with JKH's own Q1 FY2026/27 chairperson's commentary about Middle East conflict disruption hitting its Maldivian Resorts portfolio hardest.

interim_updates.note_text: John Keells Hotels (Cinnamon Hotels & Resorts) posted Rs.5.18bn revenue for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), down 17% YoY, with the Group's operating loss widening more than six-fold (Rs.181mn to Rs.1.33bn) and the loss before tax widening 125% (Rs.861mn to Rs.1.94bn). Loss attributable to equity holders was Rs.1.70bn (EPS -Rs.1.17) versus Rs.756mn (EPS -Rs.0.52) a year earlier -- despite a larger tax reversal (Rs.240mn vs Rs.105mn) partly offsetting the pre-tax loss. The operating-segment note shows this is almost entirely a Maldives story: Maldives revenue fell 24% YoY (Rs.3.98bn to Rs.3.01bn) and the Maldives segment loss widened roughly 13-fold (Rs.87mn to Rs.1.18bn), while Sri Lanka revenue fell a milder 6% and its segment loss widened more modestly (Rs.127mn to Rs.197mn). This matches parent JKH's own Q1 FY2026/27 commentary attributing softer Leisure performance to Middle East conflict disruption hitting the Maldivian Resorts portfolio hardest, given its greater reliance on source markets that travel via the Middle East.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison is possible: this filing discloses only the current quarter (30 June 2026) against the same quarter a year earlier (30 June 2025), not the immediately preceding quarter (31 March 2026) income statement -- only balance sheet figures as at 31 March 2026 are given as a second comparative column, not a full income statement. The 'Tax (Reversal)/Expense' metric above is a tax credit in both periods (not a normal expense); a bigger negative value means a larger favourable credit, so it is marked 'improved' even though the raw percentage change is negative under the standard formula.
interim_updates.takeaway: A clean, single-cause story confirmed by both this filing's own segment note and parent JKH's separately-filed commentary: the Maldives resorts business, not Sri Lanka operations, drove almost all of the YoY loss-widening, consistent with reduced travel demand from Middle East conflict disruption. No QoQ comparison is possible since only the prior-year quarter is disclosed here.
operational_highlights: Group revenue Rs.5.18bn, down 17% YoY; operating loss widened to Rs.1.33bn (from Rs.181mn); loss before tax Rs.1.94bn (+125% wider YoY)
Loss attributable to equity holders Rs.1.70bn (EPS -Rs.1.17) vs Rs.756mn (EPS -Rs.0.52) a year earlier
Maldives segment: revenue -24% YoY (Rs.3.98bn to Rs.3.01bn), segment loss widened from Rs.87mn to Rs.1.18bn -- the dominant driver of the Group result
Sri Lanka segment: revenue -6% YoY, segment loss widened more modestly (Rs.127mn to Rs.197mn)
Company (standalone) PAT Rs.22.3mn, up 78% YoY, driven by higher finance income (Rs.53.1mn vs Rs.24.0mn) rather than any operating business (holding company has no revenue)
key_drivers: The YoY loss-widening is concentrated almost entirely in the Maldives segment (loss up ~13x), not Sri Lanka (loss up ~1.6x) -- a geographic concentration, not a broad operational deterioration

This aligns with parent JKH's own Q1 FY2026/27 interim commentary, which attributes softer Leisure performance to Middle East conflict disruption to travel demand, 'with the effect being more pronounced across the Group's Maldivian Resorts portfolio' due to greater reliance on source markets that travel via the Middle East
A larger tax reversal (Rs.240mn vs Rs.105mn YoY) partially offset the pre-tax loss widening, keeping the bottom-line loss growth (125%) roughly in line with the pre-tax loss growth rather than worse

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
